nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What insights do the findings about frost damage provide?
nodes.answer: The findings offer insight into the causes of frost damage, which is vital for the design and assessment of concrete structures in frost-prone environments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the effect of pre-damage on splitting tensile strength compared to internal frost damage alone?
nodes.answer: The interaction between pre-damage and frost damage significantly reduced splitting tensile strength compared to internal frost damage alone.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What has increased the risk of frost damage to concrete structures in cold regions?
nodes.answer: Recent climate change has increased the frequency of Freeze-Thaw Cycles (FTCs), escalating the risk for existing concrete structures.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What happens to ice confined within the pore system of concrete during the freezing phase of Freeze-Thaw Cycles (FTCs)?
nodes.answer: Ice expands, inducing tensile stresses that form micro-cracks and interconnect pores.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What can occur concurrently with internal frost damage in concrete components?
nodes.answer: Cracks may occur concurrently with internal frost damage or develop beforehand.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_005
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the names and identification numbers of the three Arctic locations managed by the Norwegian Centre for Climate Services in Svalbard?
nodes.answer: The three locations are Bjørnøya (No. SN99710), Ny-Ålesund (No. SN99910), and Svalbard Lufthavn (No. SN99840).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_006
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What characteristic soils dominate the non-subglacial polar lands, and where do they occur?
nodes.answer: The characteristic permafrost soils dominate the non-subglacial polar lands and occur sporadically in sub-Arctic or non-Arctic alpine regions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was monitored throughout the Freeze-Thaw Cycle procedure?
nodes.answer: Temperature changes throughout the FTC procedure were monitored by electronic probes embedded in the concrete.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_008
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Which Arctic stations were analyzed for extreme precipitation in this study?
nodes.answer: The Arctic stations analyzed were Bjørnøya, Ny-Ålesund, and Svalbard Lufthavn.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What threshold must the saturation of concrete exceed for internal frost damage to occur?
nodes.answer: Internal frost damage occurs only when the saturation of concrete exceeds a critical threshold, as per theories proposed by Fagerlund.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Melting permafrost and landslides_qna_010
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is one of the major types of damage caused by freeze-thaw cycles in concrete?
nodes.answer: One of the major types of damage caused by freeze-thaw cycles in concrete is internal frost damage.
